import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='weight_grams', # Use weight to indicate size for an additional dimension
    sizes=(20, 400), # Adjust size range for better visibility
    alpha=0.7,
    palette='viridis' # Choose a color palette
)

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type and Weight', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend title for 'size'
handles, labels = scatter_plot.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Find the index for the 'Weight (grams)' legend part
weight_legend_idx = labels.index('weight_grams')
labels[weight_legend_idx] = 'Weight (grams)' # Rename the label
plt.legend(handles=handles, labels=labels, title='Sensor Type / Weight', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
